Natural_Language: General provisions on foreign acquisition: Buy American restricts non-domestic supplies and requires domestic construction materials; trade agreements provide exceptions; country of origin tests differ by statute.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_001_a (Buy American restrictions); P_25_001_b (trade agreement exceptions); P_25_001_c (country of origin test differences)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three main provisions of Part 25 general section. All three operate concurrently.

Natural_Language: 41 U.S.C. chapter 83, Buy American: (1) restricts purchase of non-domestic end products for use within the United States, with exceptions; and (2) requires use of only domestic construction materials in U.S. construction contracts, with some exceptions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_001_a_1 (supply restriction); P_25_001_a_2 (construction material requirement)
Validation_Notes: Parent combining the two primary Buy American restrictions. Both apply simultaneously under the statute.

Natural_Language: 41 U.S.C. chapter 83 restricts the purchase of supplies that are not domestic end products for use within the United States. A foreign end product may be purchased if the contracting officer determines that the price of the lowest domestic offer is unreasonable or if another exception applies (see subpart 25.1).
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_001_a_1_a (restriction on non-domestic supplies); P_25_001_a_1_b (unreasonable price exception); P_25_001_a_1_c (other exceptions per subpart 25.1)
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Default restriction with conditional exceptions. Rule 15 used for the exception pathway. The negation of the restriction triggers exception analysis. Either unreasonable cost or other exception sufficient.

Natural_Language: 41 U.S.C. chapter 83 requires, with some exceptions, the use of only domestic construction materials in contracts for construction in the United States (see subpart 25.2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_001_a_2_a (domestic construction material requirement); P_25_001_a_2_b (exceptions per subpart 25.2)
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement with conditional exception pathway. Rule 15 for exception trigger. Exceptions negate the domestic-only requirement for specific materials.

Natural_Language: The restrictions in the Buy American statute are not applicable in acquisitions subject to certain trade agreements (see subpart 25.4). End products and construction materials from certain countries receive nondiscriminatory treatment. The dollar value of the acquisition determines which trade agreement applies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_001_b_a (trade agreement applicability negates BA restrictions); P_25_001_b_b (nondiscriminatory treatment for designated countries); P_25_001_b_c (dollar value determines applicable agreement)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Trade agreement applicability is a conditional that negates Buy American restrictions entirely. Rule 15 for the conditional structure. Multiple consequents joined by conjunction.

Natural_Language: The test to determine country of origin for an end product differs between the Buy American statute, trade agreements, and the representation at 52.225-18.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_001_c_1 (BA two-part test); P_25_001_c_2 (trade agreement substantial transformation test); P_25_001_c_3 (52.225-18 place of manufacture test)
Validation_Notes: Parent identifying three distinct origin tests. All three exist concurrently in different regulatory contexts.

Natural_Language: The Buy American statute uses a two-part test to define a domestic end product or domestic construction material: manufactured in the United States and a domestic content test. The domestic content test has been waived for COTS items, except products consisting wholly or predominantly of iron or steel (excluding COTS fasteners).
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_001_c_1_a (manufactured in U.S.); P_25_001_c_1_b (domestic content test); P_25_001_c_1_c (COTS waiver); P_25_001_c_1_d (iron/steel exception to COTS waiver)
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two-part test with COTS waiver and iron/steel exception to the waiver. Multiple conditional layers. Rule 15 for both the waiver and exception-to-waiver conditionals.

Natural_Language: Under the trade agreements, the test to determine country of origin is substantial transformation (i.e., transforming an article into a new and different article of commerce with a name, character, or use distinct from the original article).
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_001_c_2 (substantial transformation test for trade agreements)
Validation_Notes: Simple conditional: trade agreement context triggers use of substantial transformation test. Rule 15 for conditional.

Natural_Language: For the representation at 52.225-18, the only criterion is whether the place of manufacture of an end product is in the United States or outside the United States, without regard to the origin of the components.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_001_c_3 (place of manufacture criterion only for 52.225-18)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Representation context triggers simplified test. Component origin explicitly irrelevant. Rule 15 for the conditional.

Natural_Language: Caribbean Basin country means any of the following countries: Antigua and Barbuda, Aruba, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bonaire, British Virgin Islands, Curacao, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Haiti, Jamaica, Montserrat, Saba, St. Kitts and Nevis, St. Lucia, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Sint Eustatius, Sint Maarten, or Trinidad and Tobago.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_CBC (enumerated list of Caribbean Basin countries)
Formal_Logic_Statement: CBC <-> (Antigua_Barbuda v Aruba v Bahamas v Barbados v Belize v Bonaire v BVI v Curacao v Dominica v Grenada v Guyana v Haiti v Jamaica v Montserrat v Saba v St_Kitts_Nevis v St_Lucia v St_Vincent_Grenadines v Sint_Eustatius v Sint_Maarten v Trinidad_Tobago)
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional: a country is a CBC if and only if it is on this list. Exhaustive enumeration.

Natural_Language: Caribbean Basin country end product means an article that meets origin and duty-free requirements.

Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional: must meet origin test AND not be excluded from duty-free treatment. Scope includes incidental services.

Natural_Language: Article is wholly the growth, product, or manufacture of a Caribbean Basin country; or has been substantially transformed in a CBC into a new and different article of commerce with a name, character, or use distinct from the original.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_CBC_EP_1_i_a (wholly CBC origin); P_25_003_CBC_EP_1_i_b (substantially transformed in CBC)
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive origin test: either wholly CBC or substantially transformed in CBC. Standard trade agreement origin pattern.

Natural_Language: Article is not excluded from duty-free treatment for Caribbean countries under 19 U.S.C. 2703(b). Excluded articles: tuna in airtight containers, petroleum products, certain watches/watch parts with column 2 country materials, certain textiles/apparel/footwear/leather goods.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_CBC_EP_1_ii_a (tuna exclusion); P_25_003_CBC_EP_1_ii_b (petroleum exclusion); P_25_003_CBC_EP_1_ii_c (watch/parts exclusion); P_25_003_CBC_EP_1_ii_d (textiles/apparel exclusion)

Justification_Rules: Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8; De Morgan's (DeM): Rule 11
Validation_Notes: Negation of disjunctive exclusion list. Article must not fall into any excluded category. HTSUS access noted for determining specific item status.

Natural_Language: Refers to a product offered for purchase under a supply contract, but for purposes of calculating the value of the acquisition, includes services (except transportation services) incidental to the article, provided that the value of those incidental services does not exceed that of the article itself.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_CBC_EP_2_a (supply contract scope); P_25_003_CBC_EP_2_b (incidental services included); P_25_003_CBC_EP_2_c (transportation excluded); P_25_003_CBC_EP_2_d (services value cap)
Validation_Notes: Scope definition with multiple conjunctive conditions. Transportation exclusion is a negation within the conjunction.

Natural_Language: Civil aircraft and related articles means: (1) all aircraft other than DoD or Coast Guard; (2) engines and parts for those aircraft; (3) other parts, components, subassemblies; and (4) ground flight simulators and parts, whether original or replacement, without regard to duty-free status under Trade Agreements Act section 601(a)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_civil_aircraft_a (non-DoD/CG aircraft); P_25_003_civil_aircraft_b (engines/parts); P_25_003_civil_aircraft_c (other parts/components); P_25_003_civil_aircraft_d (simulators/parts)
Formal_Logic_Statement: P_25_003_civil_aircraft <-> (P_25_003_civil_aircraft_a v P_25_003_civil_aircraft_b v P_25_003_civil_aircraft_c v P_25_003_civil_aircraft_d)
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional with disjunctive scope. Any of the four categories qualifies.

Natural_Language: Component means an article, material, or supply incorporated directly into an end product or construction material.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_component (single atomic)
Formal_Logic_Statement: Component <-> (Article v Material v Supply) ^ DirectlyIncorporated ^ (EndProduct v ConstructionMaterial)
Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional. Three types of items (disjunctive), directly incorporated (conjunctive qualifier), into one of two product types (disjunctive).

Natural_Language: Construction material means an article, material, or supply brought to the construction site by a contractor or subcontractor for incorporation into the building or work. Includes preassembled items. Emergency life safety systems evaluated as single distinct construction material. Government-purchased materials are supplies, not construction material.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_construction_material_a (brought to site for incorporation); P_25_003_construction_material_b (preassembled items included); P_25_003_construction_material_c (emergency life safety as single material); P_25_003_construction_material_d (govt purchases are supplies not CM)
Validation_Notes: Definitional conjunction with negation for the government-purchase exclusion. Emergency life safety clause is a special aggregation rule.

Natural_Language: Cost of components: (1) for purchased components, acquisition cost including transportation and duty; (2) for manufactured components, all manufacturing costs plus transportation plus allocable overhead, excluding profit. Does not include end product manufacturing costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_cost_of_components_1 (purchased); P_25_003_cost_of_components_2 (manufactured)
Validation_Notes: Two mutually exclusive calculation methods based on whether component is purchased or manufactured.

Natural_Language: For components purchased by the contractor, the acquisition cost, including transportation costs to the place of incorporation into the end product or construction material (whether or not such costs are paid to a domestic firm), and any applicable duty (whether or not a duty-free entry certificate is issued).
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_cost_of_components_1_a (acquisition cost); P_25_003_cost_of_components_1_b (transportation included regardless of payee); P_25_003_cost_of_components_1_c (duty included regardless of certificate)
Validation_Notes: Conditional: if purchased, cost includes all three elements. Rule 15 for conditional trigger. Parenthetical qualifiers clarify that domestic payee status and duty-free certificates are irrelevant.

Natural_Language: For components manufactured by the contractor, all costs associated with the manufacture of the component, including transportation costs, plus allocable overhead costs, but excluding profit. Cost of components does not include any costs associated with the manufacture of the end product.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_cost_of_components_2_a (manufacturing costs); P_25_003_cost_of_components_2_b (transportation); P_25_003_cost_of_components_2_c (allocable overhead); P_25_003_cost_of_components_2_d (profit excluded); P_25_003_cost_of_components_2_e (end product mfg costs excluded)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional: if manufactured, cost includes three elements and excludes two. Rule 15 for conditional. Two explicit exclusions as negations.

Natural_Language: Critical component means a component that is mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States and deemed critical to the U.S. supply chain. The list of critical components is at 25.105.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_critical_component (single atomic)
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional with two conjunctive conditions. List maintained at 25.105.

Natural_Language: Critical item means a domestic construction material or domestic end product that is deemed critical to the U.S. supply chain. The list of critical items is at 25.105.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_critical_item (single atomic)

Formal_Logic_Statement: DesignatedCountry <-> (P_25_003_designated_country_1 v P_25_003_designated_country_2 v P_25_003_designated_country_3 v P_25_003_designated_country_4)

Natural_Language: Least developed countries: Afghanistan, Angola, Bangladesh, Benin, Bhutan, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Democratic Republic of Congo, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Haiti, Kiribati, Laos, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Nepal, Niger, Rwanda, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, Timor-Leste, Togo, Tuvalu, Uganda, Vanuatu, Yemen, or Zambia.

Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_designated_country_4 (CBC enumeration)
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference to CBC definition. Same enumerated list.

Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_dom_const_mat_1 (non-iron/steel test); P_25_003_dom_const_mat_2 (iron/steel test)
Validation_Notes: Parent definition splitting into two mutually exclusive material-type paths.

Natural_Language: For construction material that does not consist wholly or predominantly of iron or steel: (i) unmanufactured and mined or produced in U.S.; or (ii) manufactured in U.S. with domestic component cost exceeding 60% (65% for 2024-2028, 75% starting 2029), or COTS. Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_dom_const_mat_1_a (unmanufactured/mined in US); P_25_003_dom_const_mat_1_b (manufactured in US + content threshold); P_25_003_dom_const_mat_1_c (COTS exemption); P_25_003_dom_const_mat_1_d (nonavailability components domestic); P_25_003_dom_const_mat_1_e (unknown origin foreign)

Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7

Natural_Language: For construction material that consists wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both, a construction material manufactured in the United States if the cost of foreign iron and steel constitutes less than 5 percent of the cost of all components. Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_dom_const_mat_2_a (manufactured in US); P_25_003_dom_const_mat_2_b (foreign iron/steel < 5%); P_25_003_dom_const_mat_2_c (cost calculation scope); P_25_003_dom_const_mat_2_d (unknown origin foreign)
Validation_Notes: Conditional on iron/steel status. Stricter test: 5% foreign content cap. No COTS waiver except for fasteners. Rule 15 for conditional.

Natural_Language: Domestic end product definition with separate tests for iron/steel vs. non-iron/steel end products.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_dom_EP_1 (non-iron/steel test); P_25_003_dom_EP_2 (iron/steel test)
Validation_Notes: Parent definition splitting into two mutually exclusive material-type paths. Parallel structure to domestic construction material.

Natural_Language: For an end product that does not consist wholly or predominantly of iron or steel: (i) unmanufactured and mined or produced in U.S.; or (ii) manufactured in U.S. with domestic component cost exceeding 60% (65% for 2024-2028, 75% starting 2029), with nonavailability-determined foreign components treated as domestic, unknown origin as foreign, U.S.-generated scrap as domestic; or COTS.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_dom_EP_1_a (unmanufactured/mined in US); P_25_003_dom_EP_1_b (manufactured in US + content threshold); P_25_003_dom_EP_1_c (COTS exemption); P_25_003_dom_EP_1_d (nonavailability components domestic); P_25_003_dom_EP_1_e (unknown origin foreign); P_25_003_dom_EP_1_f (US scrap domestic)
Formal_Logic_Statement: ~IronSteel -> ((P_25_003_dom_EP_1_a v (ManufacturedUS ^ ContentThreshold) v COTS) ^ P_25_003_dom_EP_1_d ^ P_25_003_dom_EP_1_e ^ P_25_003_dom_EP_1_f)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Parallel structure to dom_const_mat_1 with addition of scrap provision. Same escalating thresholds. Rule 15 for conditional. Alternate percentage possible per FAR 25.101(d).

Natural_Language: For an end product that consists wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both, manufactured in United States if cost of foreign iron and steel constitutes less than 5 percent of cost of all components. Cost includes foreign mill products, castings, forgings, and estimate of foreign iron/steel components excluding COTS fasteners. Unknown origin treated as foreign. Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_dom_EP_2_a (manufactured in US); P_25_003_dom_EP_2_b (foreign iron/steel < 5%); P_25_003_dom_EP_2_c (cost calculation scope); P_25_003_dom_EP_2_d (unknown origin foreign)
Validation_Notes: Parallel structure to dom_const_mat_2. Same 5% foreign content cap for iron/steel products. Rule 15 for conditional.

Natural_Language: Domestic offer means an offer of a domestic end product. When the solicitation specifies award on a group of line items, a domestic offer means an offer where the proposed price of the domestic end products exceeds 50 percent of the total proposed price of the group.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_dom_offer_a (single item: offer of domestic EP); P_25_003_dom_offer_b (group award: domestic EP price > 50% of group total)
Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional with two alternative tests depending on award structure.

Natural_Language: Eligible offer means an offer of an eligible product. Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_eligible_offer_a (single item: offer of eligible product); P_25_003_eligible_offer_b (group award: eligible + domestic EP price > 50% of group total)
Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional. Group award test requires foreign offer status AND combined price threshold.

Natural_Language: Eligible product means a foreign end product, construction material, or service that, due to applicability of a trade agreement to a particular acquisition, is not subject to discriminatory treatment.

Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional. Three eligible categories (disjunctive), trade agreement applicability (conjunctive), non-discrimination (negation).

Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7

Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_fastener (single atomic)

Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_foreign_const_mat (single atomic)

Natural_Language: Foreign contractor means a contractor or subcontractor organized or existing under the laws of a country other than the United States.

Natural_Language: Foreign offer means any offer other than a domestic offer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_foreign_offer (single atomic)
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional via negation. Binary classification.

Atomic_Propositions: P_25_003_FTA_country (enumerated list)
